This supports an acute eczema flare with severe pruritus in those areas, despite the doctor mentioning back once.
Patient explicitly connects itch to sleep disturbance: 'I can't even sleep at night' in context of 'it's itching a lot, like all the time,' supporting that pruritus is causing sleep disturbance.

Doctor says 'giving you a stronger prescription of a of a steroid may be beneficial, which I'm happy to prescribe to you today' and to use treatments 'for the first seven to ten days,' but there is no mention of 'twice daily' application or explicit duration of steroid itself; 7–10 days timeframe is for treatment overall. Frequency is an added detail.

Doctor: 'I'm going to give you something, some emollients, which helps to moisturize the skin... which use in the bath and shower. And it's definitely worth um using that for the first seven to ten days.' This supports emollient wash/moisturizer use, especially with bathing.
Doctor: 'I can give you something a little bit stronger today as well. Um, something like Fexofenadine, which I can give to you today.' This is an oral antihistamine for itch.

Doctor advises: 'it's also worth keeping a diary of any triggers which are affecting your symptoms, anything you wear or anything you use, in terms of shower gels or soap.' This matches keeping a trigger diary including soaps and clothing.

Doctor: 'using the steroids and the emollients... over the next week to ten days, should hopefully control your symptoms. But do come back and see me next week, if things don't get better.' This supports follow-up in about a week if no improvement or worsening.
